Name: Enchanted Clothing
Author: poaskkiliaks
Description:
[b][color=#d4d4d8][size=6]Enchanted Clothing[/size][/color][/b]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[i]Bind a ring's power to what you wear, at the sewing machine.[/i]

Rings are the best gear in the game and you only ever get to wear two. [b]Enchanted Clothing[/b] lets you sew a ring into a shirt, a pair of pants, a hat or your boots: the garment keeps the ring's power for as long as you wear it, and the ring can be taken back out whenever you want it elsewhere.

[/color]
[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]How it works[/b][/size]

At any sewing machine — Emily and Haley's, or your own — put the garment in the left slot (the spool, the same place you'd put clothing to dye it) and the ring in the right slot:

[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Garment + ring[/b] — the piece comes out enchanted. The ring is consumed and [b]1 Cloth[/b] is spent from your inventory.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Enchanted garment + another ring[/b] — the new ring is bound and the [b]old ring is handed back[/b] to you.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Enchanted garment + Cloth[/b] — the enchantment breaks and the [b]ring is returned intact[/b].[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]
While the piece is worn, its ring behaves exactly like a ring on your finger: stat bonuses, Glow Ring light, Slime Charmer immunity, Burglar's Ring drops, Napalm explosions, Phoenix revives, and so on. Combined rings from the Forge keep every ring inside them.

Shirt, pants, hat and boots each hold one ring, so a full outfit is worth four extra ring slots. Each slot can be switched off in the settings if that's more than you want.

[/color]
[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Telling an enchanted piece apart[/b][/size]
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8]A sparkle pulses on the item's icon in your inventory.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]The tooltip ends with [b]Enchanted: <ring name>[/b], written in that ring's own colour — prismatic and shifting for combined rings.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]While worn, the piece gives off faint sparkles in the same colour.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Notes[/b][/size]
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8]Clothing that can't be dyed can still be enchanted — the sewing machine normally turns those away.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]An enchanted garment can't be dyed white with Cloth, because that pair unbinds the ring instead. Take the ring out, dye it, then bind the ring again.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Selling or trashing an enchanted piece destroys the ring with it.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Rings worn on your fingers can't be dropped into the machine — take the ring off first.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Boots still work as usual in the machine: boots + boots copies stats, since that pair involves no ring.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]With [b]Item Bags[/b] installed, Cloth stored in a bag counts toward the cost and is taken straight out of it, including bags tucked inside an Omni Bag.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Combat overhauls that rewrite the game's damage handling can drop vanilla's Slime Charmer check; this mod applies that rule itself so the effect still works through clothing.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Configuration[/b][/size]
Everything can be adjusted in-game with [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b], or in [font=Courier New]config.json[/font]:
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Allow Pants / Hats / Boots[/b] — which slots can be enchanted. Shirts always can.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Cloth Cost[/b] — how much Cloth binding a ring costs (0 to make it free).[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][b]Magic Sparkles[/b] and [b]Sparkle on Icon[/b] — the visual markers, if you'd rather play without them.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Console commands[/b][/size]
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8][font=Courier New]ec_status[/font] — lists what you're wearing, what each piece is enchanted with, and whether the ring effects are active.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][font=Courier New]ec_enchant <ring id> [shirt|pants|hat|boots][/font] — binds a ring directly, e.g. [font=Courier New]ec_enchant 517 hat[/font].[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8][font=Courier New]ec_disenchant[/font] — strips the enchantments from everything you're wearing and returns the rings.[/color][/*]
[/list]

[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8]SMAPI 4.0.0 or later[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Generic Mod Config Menu (optional, for in-game settings)[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Item Bags (optional — lets the cloth cost come out of your bags)[/color][/*]
[/list]

[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]
Safe to add to an existing save. The bound ring is stored on the garment itself, so removing the mod simply leaves ordinary clothing behind — take your rings back out first if you want to keep them.

[/color]
[line]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[size=5][b]Changelog[/b][/size]

[b]1.1.0[/b] — first public release
[/color]
[list]

[*][color=#D4D4D8]Enchant shirts, pants, hats and boots with any ring at the sewing machine, and unbind the ring later to get it back.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Cloth stored in Item Bags (including inside Omni Bags) can pay for the enchantment.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Enchanted pieces are marked with a sparkling icon, a coloured tooltip line and sparkles while worn.[/color][/*]
[/list]

Manifest.Name: Enchanted Clothing
Manifest.Description: Enchant your clothes with the power of a ring at the sewing machine. Spend a cloth to bind any ring to a shirt, pants, hat or boots, wear the ring's effect without using a finger slot, and unbind it later to get the ring back.
Manifest.Author: Lazy Mug
